meta.description: Weekly lawn mowing in Fenton, MI by Grand Scapes: mowed, trimmed, edged and blown off on a set day, on sandy city lots and soft lakefront lawns alike.

hero.title: A clean cut, **lake to curb.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes mows Fenton lawns every week on a set day: mowed, trimmed, edged along each walk and curb, and blown off. Sandy rises, soft lakefront yards and big township lots each get a plan that fits the ground.

local.title: Two kinds of ground, **one mowing day.**
local.intro: Lawns here do not all grow the same way. The soil survey maps sandy, well drained Boyer and Wawasee soils on the rises in and around the city, and wetter Conover loam and muck down by the lakes in the township. Sand runs dry first in a hot July. Muck stays soft for days after a rain. Mowing well means reading the ground, not just the calendar.

points.title: Keep the deck up on sand
points.body: MSU Extension's lawn tip sheet says to mow at least 3 inches high, because taller grass shades the soil and grows deeper roots. On a sandy lot that dries out fast, that extra height is often the difference between green and straw by August.

points.title: Clippings stay out of the lake
points.body: MSU's advice is to never discharge clippings near lakes, rivers, streams or drains. On a lakefront lawn we blow clippings back onto the grass and off the drive, and never toward the water or the storm drain at the curb.

points.title: A clean line at the shore
points.body: If you keep a strip of taller native plants along the water, as MSU recommends to protect the shoreline, we mow a crisp edge to it and leave the strip alone. A clean line between lawn and buffer looks planned, not forgotten.

points.title: Soft ground after a rain
points.body: On muck and wet loam near the lakes, a heavy mower can rut a lawn that looks fine from the drive. If a low corner is still soft on your day, we trim it by hand and catch it next week rather than leave tracks across it.

logistics.title: Your mowing day, and the full job every visit.
body: Fenton lawns go on a fixed day of the week. Every visit is the whole job: mowed, trimmed around beds, trees and the mailbox, edged along the curb and the walks, and blown off so the drive is clean when you pull in.

Rob comes out for the estimate, looks at the size of the lawn, the slopes and the gates, and gives you a weekly price before the first cut. If the yard has a dog that must stay in, a locked gate or a path down to the lake, tell us once and the crew will know.

Come fall, the mowing rolls into [leaf removal](/leaf-removal-fenton-mi/). In spring, a [spring cleanup](/spring-cleanup-fenton-mi/) clears winter debris and gets the yard ready for the first mow of the year.

faq.q: Who mows lawns weekly in Fenton, MI?
faq.a: Grand Scapes does. We mow lawns in the City of Fenton and in the township every week on a set day: mowed, trimmed, edged and blown off. Rob gives a free estimate after he walks the yard. Call [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040) or [text Rob](sms:+18109903040) to set one up.

faq.q: How often should my lawn be mowed in summer?
faq.a: Often enough that no more than a third of the grass blade comes off at once. That is MSU Extension's rule of thumb, and in fast spring growth it can mean every four to five days. Weekly suits most lawns here, with the cut set high enough that a week of growth does not break the rule.

faq.q: Should clippings be bagged on a lakefront lawn?
faq.a: Usually not. MSU says clippings returned to the lawn do not build thatch and should go back on the grass whenever possible. What matters on the lake is where they land: on the lawn, and off the drive, the road and the water.

faq.q: When is the last mow of the year in Fenton?
faq.a: When the grass stops growing, usually late in the fall. MSU Extension says to lower the mowing height for that final cut so the lawn does not go into winter too tall, which helps with snow mold and voles. Leaves can be mowed into the lawn on the way there; MSU studies found no harm from up to 6 inches of them.
